description:
The public log cannot group 1,382 `AnalyzeActivation` evaluations by activation,
because identity is thrown away at the projection boundary.

    jsonl.rs  write_opaque: Job -> job_kind(job), a bare variant name
    jsonl.rs  write_opaque: ProductKey -> key.kind()
    jsonl.rs  write_activation_key -> root_id + function_id, DROPS arrow

## Scope: WITHIN-run identity only

Within one process a raw `Ty` id is stable, so grouping needs nothing more than
the structural fields plus the raw arrow id. That is free -- no rendering, no
`Types` lookup.

CROSS-run comparison is a different requirement with a different answer
(fz-f98.21's faithful canonical form) and belongs to the acceptance child. Do
NOT render types through `Types::display` here as a shortcut: display is
measured NOT injective (`Ty(83)` and `Ty(253)` both render `([int]) -> r0` while
`253 <: 83`), so it would silently conflate distinct activations.

## No restructuring needed (verified against the tree)

Every payload of all five identity domains bottoms out in raw ids plus one
`String` (`TypeName.name`): Job and FactKey carry
CodeId/ModuleId/FunctionId/RootId/TypeName/ActivationKey/CallSiteKey/ExecutableKey;
ProductKey adds InputSlot and TransportPosition; TransportPosition carries
`ExecutableSymbol { function, arrow: Ty, input: Box<[Ty]> }` plus
callsite/entry ids. None of it needs `&World`/`&Types`, so identity renders in
`write_opaque` exactly where each key renders today. (An earlier revision of
this ticket claimed rendering had to move into `write_compiler2_semantic`; that
premise was wrong for within-run scope.)

The one production addition outside `jsonl.rs`: `Ty::as_u32`, matching the
existing accessor precedent on CodeId/FunctionId/ModuleId/RootId -- `Ty(u32)`
exposes only `Debug` today.

## Deliver

- Identity for `Job`, `FactKey`, `ProductKey`, `CallSiteKey`, `TransportPosition`
  on the events that carry them: variant kind plus payload ids, including the
  activation arrow everywhere an ActivationKey appears (write_activation_key
  gains `arrow`). JobCompletion renders its job's full identity, and the
  blocked-wait lists render fact identity, not bare kind strings.
- Emit sites unchanged: they keep passing raw keys plus the owning authority.
  A telemetry-disabled run must render nothing.

## Red test

Two activations of the same function are distinguishable in the public log
(via PublicTrace, fz-kdt.34.1).

## Checks

- `production_telemetry_boundaries_are_raw_and_allocation_free` (`world_test.rs:13`)
  still passes -- it scans emit-site files only, and emit sites are untouched.
- No new allocation at any emit site.
title: Render formula and product IDENTITY in the public log
